candidates.next_evidence: Track 2026 booked load factor, net yield growth, onboard revenue per passenger, new-ship delivery timing, fuel/labor cost inflation, and whether bookings remain resilient across income cohorts.
candidates.node_relation: Direct asset owner and operator of cruise capacity; exposed to packaged-value travel demand, onboard spending, itinerary pricing, and ship-delivery capacity additions.
candidates.theme_relation: Consumer discretionary experiences; cruise vacations can capture value-conscious and higher-income leisure travel demand while supply is constrained by long ship-order lead times.
candidates.why_include: Royal Caribbean is one of the obvious leaders in public cruise exposure. Its 2025 Form 10-K reported 2026 capacity growth expectations and yield performance, while S&P noted strong 2026 forward bookings at higher prices and roughly two-thirds of 2026 capacity booked. This maps directly to the node hypothesis that cruise capacity and packaged-value travel may be attractive chokepoints.

candidates.next_evidence: Verify 2026 cumulative booked position versus historical ranges, net per-diem growth, onboard spend, ship-delivery pipeline, debt refinancing costs, and whether lower-income cruise demand remains positive.
candidates.node_relation: Direct cruise-capacity owner with global brand portfolio and exposure to ticket pricing, onboard spend, deposits, and fleet deployment.
candidates.theme_relation: Consumer discretionary travel experiences; Carnival is a scale cruise supplier and a direct beneficiary or victim of cruise demand, capacity discipline, and consumer budget substitution toward all-inclusive travel.
candidates.why_include: Carnival is the largest broad public cruise-capacity exposure. Its 2025 annual report described record booking trends and record year-end customer deposits, supporting inclusion as a direct candidate for the packaged-value cruise chokepoint lane.

candidates.next_evidence: Track room-night growth, gross bookings growth, take rate, merchant versus agency mix, Genius loyalty penetration, AI-search disruption risk, and regional exposure to Europe, Asia, and U.S. inbound travel.
candidates.node_relation: Demand-aggregation platform across hotels, alternative accommodations, flights, rental cars, restaurants, and travel services; monetizes travel search, conversion, merchant payments, and loyalty engagement.
candidates.theme_relation: Consumer travel platform exposure; can benefit from secular online booking penetration, cross-sell, loyalty distribution, and fragmented lodging supply even when asset owners face mixed RevPAR trends.
candidates.why_include: Booking is an obvious leader in online travel distribution. Company factsheet data showed 2025 gross travel bookings of $186.1 billion and 1.2 billion room nights booked, making it a direct public-market mapping for the travel demand-aggregation lane.

candidates.next_evidence: Track 2026 event-market booking curves, ADR equivalent trends, host supply growth, urban regulation risk, cross-border travel demand, Experiences relaunch contribution, and cancellation rates.
candidates.node_relation: Alternative-lodging marketplace that expands flexible travel accommodation supply and can capture event-driven lodging demand where hotels are constrained or expensive.
candidates.theme_relation: Consumer travel experiences and lodging supply; directly tied to nights booked, host supply, event demand, and consumer substitution between hotels and short-term rentals.
candidates.why_include: Airbnb is a direct public platform for alternative lodging. Its Q4 2025 shareholder materials reported FY2025 Nights and Seats Booked of 533.0 million and Gross Booking Value of $91.3 billion. Event-driven demand around constrained markets, including World Cup host cities, makes the platform relevant even if hotel bookings are uneven.

candidates.next_evidence: Track U.S. RevPAR by chain scale, group demand, World Cup host-city performance, Bonvoy member room-night penetration, net rooms growth, franchise fee growth, and owner economics under higher labor and financing costs.
candidates.node_relation: Asset-light global hotel brand and loyalty platform with direct exposure to RevPAR, net room growth, franchise/management fees, and event-driven lodging markets.
candidates.theme_relation: Consumer travel and lodging; Marriott maps to constrained hotel supply, loyalty distribution, group/transient travel, and World Cup or event calendar upside, while also testing whether hotel RevPAR can outpace inflation.
candidates.why_include: Marriott is an obvious leader in hotel distribution and loyalty. Its FY2025 results reported nearly 271 million Marriott Bonvoy members at year-end and guided to 2026 worldwide RevPAR growth and net rooms growth, making it a direct candidate for hotel supply and loyalty-distribution exposure.

evidence.claim: U.S. Travel Association's Spring 2026 forecast projects total U.S. travel spending of about $1.374 trillion in 2026 and $1.420 trillion in 2027, with international spending forecast to recover modestly after a 2025 decline.
CoStar and Tourism Economics upgraded their June 2026 U.S. hotel outlook, citing stronger-than-expected demand and raising the 2026 U.S. RevPAR growth forecast to 2.8%.
evidence.source_title: U.S. Hotel Forecast Assumptions – June 2026 | CoStar

evidence.claim: Recent reporting cited Bank of America data showing U.S. cruise spending rose across income groups in the first four months of 2026 versus the prior year, supporting the hypothesis that cruises remain resilient packaged-value experiences.

Royal Caribbean's 2025 Form 10-K reported 2025 net yield growth and expected 2026 capacity growth of 6.7% versus 2025, tied to new ships including Star of the Seas, Celebrity Xcel, and Legend of the Seas.
S&P Global Ratings stated that Royal Caribbean reported good 2026 forward bookings at higher prices and had approximately two-thirds of 2026 capacity booked.
evidence.source_title: Research Update: Royal Caribbean Cruises Ltd. Upgraded

evidence.claim: Carnival's 2025 annual report described record booking trends, strong close-in demand, and record year-end customer deposits up nearly 7% year over year.
Booking Holdings reported 2025 gross travel bookings of $186.1 billion and 1.2 billion room nights booked.
Airbnb reported FY2025 Nights and Seats Booked of 533.0 million and Gross Booking Value of $91.3 billion.
Marriott reported nearly 271 million Marriott Bonvoy members at year-end 2025, U.S. member stays accounting for 75% of room nights, and 2026 guidance for worldwide RevPAR and net rooms growth.
evidence.source_title: Marriott International Reports Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2025 Results

evidence.claim: World Cup lodging impact remains uneven: AP reported in May 2026 that hotel operators in several U.S. host cities said bookings were running behind typical seasonal demand, which is a falsification risk for event-driven lodging upside.
evidence.source_title: US hotel operators say promised boon from hosting World Cup hasn't materialized yet

memory_update.text: RCL and CCL are the cleanest direct public mappings for cruise-capacity and packaged-value travel exposure; prioritize evidence on 2026 booked position, net yields, onboard spend, and capacity additions.

BKNG and ABNB map to demand aggregation rather than owned physical capacity; they may benefit from fragmented travel supply, loyalty or repeat behavior, event-driven lodging, and online booking share, but require monitoring for AI-search and regulation risks.

MAR represents hotel brand, franchise, and loyalty distribution exposure rather than pure hotel real estate ownership; it is suitable for tracking RevPAR, Bonvoy penetration, and event-market lodging data.

The travel-experience-capacity node should be split in later layers into cruise capacity, hotel brand/loyalty distribution, alternative lodging supply, OTA demand aggregation, airlines, attractions/theme parks, ticketing, luggage, and travel payments.

Not included due to the 5-candidate limit but relevant for future passes: Expedia, Hilton, Hyatt, Choice Hotels, Wyndham, Host Hotels, Vail Resorts, Disney parks, United/Delta/American/Southwest, Live Nation, and payment/network beneficiaries such as Visa, Mastercard, and Global Payments.

World Cup lodging upside is not a settled fact. Recent sources show improved general U.S. hotel forecasts but mixed World Cup-specific booking evidence; future research should separate broad RevPAR recovery from host-city event spikes.

node: Travel experiences: cruises, hotels, online travel platforms, airlines, attractions, and event-driven lodging
summary: Expanded the direct public-company universe for travel-experience capacity. The highest-confidence candidates are cruise operators with constrained physical capacity and strong booking curves, online travel platforms aggregating lodging and experience demand, alternative-lodging supply aggregators, and asset-light hotel brand/loyalty platforms. This pass excludes weaker undifferentiated airline capacity and focuses on companies where demand aggregation, packaged-value travel, loyalty distribution, or lodging supply can plausibly create pricing power or operating leverage.
